# Book of Giants Fragment 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4Q532 (Cave 4) | **Condition:** very fragmentary; only scattered phrases survive

---

**7:1** [...] Ohya fought-with [...] the-beast [...]

**7:2** [...] and-he-grasped the-wild-beast [...] and-struck-it [...]

**7:3** [...] and-wrestled with-it upon the-ground [...]

**7:4** [...] and-the-beast was-mighty [...] but-Ohya prevailed [...]

**7:5** [...] and-he-grasped the-wild-beast and-its-horns [...]

**7:6** [...] and-he-struck-it and-killed-it [...]

**7:7** [...] and-the-giants rejoiced over-the-slaying [...]

**7:8** [...] and-they-feasted upon-its-flesh [...]

**7:9** [...] but-the-killing brought no-peace [...]

**7:10** [...] for-the-judgment still approached [...]

**7:11** [...] Gilgamesh [...] and-the-giants [...] in-contest [...]

**7:12** [...] and-he-was-mighty among-them [...] a-warrior [...]

**7:13** [...] and-the-battle-was great [...]

**7:14** [...] and-the-noise reached to-heaven [...]

**7:15** [...] and-they-fought-together [...] giant against-giant [...]

**7:16** [...] and-they-fought together [...]

**7:17** [...] and-the-earth shook under-their-feet [...]

**7:18** [...] and-dust rose to-the-clouds [...]

**7:19** [...] but-none could-prevail against-the-other [...]

**7:20** [...] for-their-strength was-equal [...]

---

*EMET notes: Fragment 7 (The Battle of the Giants). Source: 4Q532. Aramaic text from Cave 4 Qumran. Hyphenated compounds preserve Aramaic construct-chain syntax and bound morphemes. Square brackets indicate genuine manuscript lacunae where the leather has deteriorated or broken away. The Book of Giants is an Aramaic expansion of the Watcher myth from 1 Enoch 6-16, featuring the Nephilim giants Ohya, Hahya (sons of Shemihazah), Mahaway (son of Baraq'el), and the hero Gilgamesh.*
